summary: A free California Campfire Permit is required before you may have a campfire, camp stove, lantern or barbeque -- but holding one does NOT mean fires are allowed where you're going. Local restrictions override it. Two different permits exist; for everywhere this project covers, take the one for federal- and state-controlled lands, not the private-lands one.
detail: TWO PERMIT TYPES, and the wrong one is not a valid document. CAL FIRE issues one permit for federal- and state-controlled lands, covering campfires, barbeques and portable stoves, and a separate one for private lands, which additionally requires written permission from the landowner. Both carry the same caveat that local burn restrictions may apply. Every trailhead in this project sits on federal land -- national forest, national park, BLM, or the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit -- except two on East Bay Regional Park District land (Del Valle and Stanford Ave), which is a special district fitting neither category cleanly; which permit applies there is not confirmed. The same portal also issues permits for burning debris, which is a different product and not what a backcountry traveller needs. THE PERMIT IS A PRECONDITION, NOT AN AUTHORISATION: CAL FIRE's own guidance says to check local rules, since many areas restrict or ban campfires outright, especially at elevation or in high fire danger. Where a wilderness bans fires, the permit still matters for a camp stove. The permits FAQ enumerates the federal/state permit as covering campfires, barbeques and portable stoves; the campfire-safety page adds lanterns, and the fuller list is kept here. The issuing forest states it is also required in some developed campgrounds -- being in a campground is not a reliable exemption. Free, valid for a full calendar year (January 1 to December 31), and available from CAL FIRE, US Forest Service or BLM offices as well as online. The signer must be 18 or older, so a group of minors cannot self-issue. Obtain it at readyforwildfire.org/permits, which links to the portal at permit.preventwildfiresca.org. NOTE: Eldorado NF's own camping page cites 'www.preventwildfiresca.org', which does not resolve -- readyforwildfire.org is the working entry point.

summary: Dispersed camping outside a developed campground is limited to 10 days per ranger district per calendar year.
detail: Most Eldorado NF land is open to free dispersed camping unless specifically prohibited. There is no trash service -- pack it in, pack it out -- and no potable water, so bring your own rather than relying on lakes, streams or springs. Remove all equipment and garbage when leaving.

summary: Campfires are prohibited year-round throughout Desolation Wilderness. Camp stoves are permitted.
detail: A stove still requires the separate California Campfire Permit that applies statewide.

summary: A hard-sided, bear-proof food storage container is REQUIRED for all food and toiletries.
detail: The permit page states the requirement without qualifying it to overnight use, and gives no elevation or zone exception; it notes bears have become more active. It says containers "may be available for rental" and to contact a Forest Service permit office, without naming terms. The specific terms below come from the 2022 USFS trip-planning guide rather than the permit page, and are the older of the two sources: fines up to $5,000 for non-compliance; canisters rent free at Placerville Ranger Station, while LTBMU rents them for a $50 deposit plus a daily fee ($5 for 1-3 days, $10 for 4-7, $15 for 8-14). Confirm rental terms before relying on them.

summary: Maximum group size is 12 people together at any time, children included in the count.
Camp on a durable surface at least 100 ft from any lakeshore or stream and from trails.
detail: Restoration sites have been closed to let damaged shorelines and meadows recover from overuse -- walk around them rather than through. Separately, four areas (Eagle Lake, Grouse and Hemlock Lakes, and the north and east sides of Lake of the Woods) allow camping only at designated sites; see data/permit_zones.csv for those zones' own rules.

summary: Human and dog waste must be packed out, or buried in a 6-8 inch cat hole at least 200 ft from water or trail. Pack out toilet paper.
detail: Wash and clean cookware at least 200 ft from any water source. Soap of any kind, biodegradable included, is prohibited in streams, lakes and any other water source. No trash service -- pack out everything you pack in.

summary: Dogs are permitted but must be under control at all times, and El Dorado County has a mandatory leash law.
detail: The agency's stated reasons for the control requirement: dogs impact wildlife, and barking intrudes on other visitors' experience. Bury or pack out dog waste on the same terms as human waste. Worth checking against neighbouring units before a multi-wilderness trip: Yosemite bans dogs from its wilderness entirely, so a dog-legal Desolation itinerary does not generalise.

summary: Livestock limited to 2 per person and 12 per group; keep them 200 ft from water and 100 ft from campsites.
detail: Do not tie stock directly to trees except briefly while loading, unloading, or resting on the move -- highline instead. Weed-free forage only. Some trails are not recommended for stock.

summary: Discharging a firearm within 150 yards of a campsite or occupied area is prohibited, as is any discharge that puts people or property at risk.
Damaging or removing any natural feature is prohibited.
detail: Photograph what you find and leave it for others.

summary: Commercial use may be prohibited or require a special use permit.
detail: Charging a fee to lead a group into the wilderness counts as outfitting and guiding and needs a special use permit -- contact a Forest Service office.

summary: Treat all water by boiling, filtering, or purification tablets.
State fish and game laws apply -- a wilderness permit is not a fishing licence.
detail: This is the whole of what the permit page says on the subject: it defers to California fish and game law without restating any of it. Season, limits, gear and licensing are set by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife and are not captured in this project, so check CDFW directly rather than treating this row as the rule.
